marks.gloss_en: our mishna: a woman may go out with strands of hair, whether her own or her friend's
why did the verse count the outer ornaments with the inner ones? to tell you: whoever gazes at a woman's little finger is as if he gazed at the place of nakedness
כדתניא: ... עד שבא רבי עקיבא ולימד: אם כן אתה מגנה על בעלה -- the concern that she not become repulsive to her husband is R' Akiva's
עד שבא רבי עקיבא ולימד: אם כן אתה מגנה על בעלה ונמצא בעלה מגרשה -- the elders' ban would make her repulsive to her husband and lead him to divorce her
[the stam: and Rav -- what is different about these?] Ulla: so that she not become repulsive to her husband
דתניא: שוטחן בחמה אבל לא כנגד העם, רבי אליעזר ורבי שמעון אוסרין -- the tannaim dispute whether it is forbidden even out of the people's view
תנאי היא -- it is a dispute of tannaim (= p_marit_ayin_tannaei_hi)
it is a dispute of tannaim [whether a marit-ha'ayin prohibition holds even out of view]
תנן: בכבול ובפאה נכרית לחצר. בשלמא לרב ניחא, אלא לרבי ענני בר ששון קשיא! -- the mishna names only the kavul and the wig for the courtyard: that fits Rav, but is difficult for R' Anani
רבי ענני בר ששון משמיה דמאן קאמר ליה? משמיה דרבי ישמעאל בר יוסי, ורבי ישמעאל בר יוסי תנא הוא ופליג -- he speaks for a tanna, who may dispute the mishna

תנן: ולא בזוג אף על פי שפקוק; ותניא אידך: פוקק לה זוג בצוארה ומטייל עמה בחצר -- what the mishna forbids going out with, the baraita permits in the courtyard (the mishna is p_chamor_zug_pakuk; see header)
another baraita: he may plug a bell on its neck and walk with it in the courtyard
with a kavul and with a foreign wig, to the courtyard
Rav: whatever the Sages forbade going out with into the public domain, one may not go out with into the courtyard
R' Anani bar Sason in R' Yishmael's name: everything is like the kavul [and may be worn into the courtyard]
Rav: wherever the Sages forbade because of marit ha'ayin, it is forbidden even in the innermost chambers
had it taught us her own [hair] only -- [permitted] because it is not repulsive; but her friend's, which is repulsive, say no -- so the friend's-hair clause is needed
and had it taught us her friend's only -- [permitted] because it is of her kind; but an animal's, which is not of her kind, say no -- so the animal's-hair clause is needed
provided an old woman does not go out with [strands of] a girl's [hair]
granted, an old woman with a girl's [hair] -- it is a praise for her
and with a totefet
with pepper, a grain of salt, and anything placed in her mouth
a false tooth, a gold tooth -- Rabbi permits [going out with it]
